additional_info.subject: RE: ID0452507-DC/Si-D/SA-[MP / RD 170003090] Charger showing Unavailable CRM:02888000280
additional_info.body:
Dear colleagues,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0452507.
The ticket has been opened by end customer Mr. Dakroury in regards of charger
MP/RD 170003090
being unavailable.
Mr. Dakroury reported that the charger is unavailable since 26.09.2025.
I checked the charger on SCB, and the charger seems offline. However, some logs are arriving (not all of them).
I checked the charger on AWS, and I see on 26.09.2025 the following error:
This is a sign of corruption of the container sicharge-cp-backend. This is a known bug related to FW v7.0.5: sometimes it can happen that, when the charger goes offline, the offline-error-flags.json file gets corrupted, resulting in an unavailable charger.
This bug was already identified in the month of August 2025, and it was communicated through several regular touchpoints from PLM and Product Champion.
The solution is to flash the CFast card to v8.0.5.
Please arrange an onsite visit in order to proceed with the CFast card flashing. What is required is:
CFast card reader
Companion Tool with FW v8.0.5 downloaded
Live Linux 2.1 USB stick - Please be aware that the configuration of the Live Linux stick can only be performed by Siemens personnel. IF this step is not possible, we will proceed with the creation of a new ChargerID on SCB.
External keyboard with USB connection.
Let me know if you require support for the onsite activity. In case yes, please plan the activity in advance coordinate with me for the remote availability.
Looking forward to hearing form you soon!
With kind regards,

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0452507-DC/Si-D/SA-[MP / RD 170003090] Charger showing Unavailable CRM:02888000280
additional_info.body:
Dear colleagues,
I am following up my previous email on case
ID0452507
bringing positive news!
Today R&D found a way to recover the
chargers where the sicharge-cp-backend is in boot loop and the charger is not accessible via SCB but sending logs.
As long as the charger does not flood with "Too many files open", R&D is able now to reach the charger via server and restore the container.
The charger
MP/RD 170003090
is now back online after R&D's intervention, and we applied also the "FileHandler" Hotfix, so to prevent this corruption to happen again.
In conclusion, the charger is now back operative, and it is not necessary anymore to go onsite and flash the CFast card.
Since the issue is solved, I will proceed to close this ticket.
Thank you!
